system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.

    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

      price-sensitive SMB accounts

    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

  PROVISIONAL DIRECTION — set by leadership before this review

    The provisional direction for this cycle is simplify_onboarding. It is
    not final: you may confirm it or replace it with any other candidate.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  1 inherited memory before committing. Name it by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memory you want verified (up to one, or none). Do not state an
action. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: The provisional direction (simplify_onboarding) rests almost entirely on memory_86, which is the single load-bearing claim for the default choice. Verifying it is the highest-value pull: if the original record shows the onboarding-shortening result was real, durable, and tied to qualified revenue rather than just completion-rate vanity metrics, that confirms the leadership direction against a live 4% onboarding decline and 6% activation decline. If it turns out to be a soft or short-horizon effect (completion and time-to-value can improve while downstream qualified revenue does not), the default collapses and I should pivot to promotional_pricing (memory_73, the direct answer to the competitor's entry pricing) or activation_messaging (memory_91). Memory_73 is the obvious alternative, but its claim is narrower and more mechanically plausible, and even if verified, a price response is defensive and risks margin and long-term revenue quality against the primary objective; verifying the default I am most likely to act on by inertia does more to change my decision. Memory_86 is also the oldest-but-most-relevant of the two overlapping activation/onboarding memories, and it partially overlaps memory_91 and memory_31, so its record may clarify whether those effects are distinct or the same lift counted three times.
